## Heavy video (all-intra conversion)

Ordinary MP4 (H.264) is compressed with reference to neighbouring frames, so playing backwards or seeking sharply makes the preview stutter. Converting every frame into a standalone image (keyframe) makes scratching smooth.

### Method A: convert with the included script (recommended)

1. Run `reascratch_reencode_mjpeg.lua` (this is also what happens if you answer Yes in the import dialog). Videos that are already all-intra are skipped (unless they are taller than the height below; then they are converted to scale them down).
   - If ffmpeg is on the PC, it is used automatically for the conversion (frames match the original one for one). Without ffmpeg, REAPER's own features are used (nothing extra to install, but cases have been seen where the picture is 1–2 frames off from the original or black frames get in). The REAPER console shows which was used.
   - Where FFmpeg is searched for: the full path in REAPER's ExtState `ReaScratch` / `ffmpeg`, the same folder as this script, REAPER's `UserPlugins` folder, `PATH`, `C:\Program Files\FFmpeg` (and its `bin`) and `C:\ffmpeg\bin` on Windows, and Homebrew on macOS (`/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`). REAPER's screen freezes during an ffmpeg conversion (it comes back when done).
2. `<name>_mjpeg.avi` is written in the same folder as the original, and the video on the track is swapped automatically (the original file is kept).
   - The height is reduced to the height chosen in setup (720, 540 or 360; default 720). When converting on import, you can choose a different height for that video only after answering Yes. Videos already smaller are not reduced (or enlarged). Files get bigger (as a guide, per minute at 30 fps: around 100 MB at 720p, 70–80 MB at 540p, 40–50 MB at 360p).
   - The cost of reading one frame (a rough guide from the PC we tested), taking 1080p as 1: about 1/2 at 720p, 1/3 at 540p, 1/6 at 360p.
   - To change the resolution or quality, open the script in a text editor and replace the right-hand side of the `local MAX_HEIGHT = …` line at the top with a number (0 keeps the original; heights other than 720, 540 and 360 also go here), or change `JPEG_QUALITY` (a number in `MAX_HEIGHT` takes priority over the height chosen in setup or on import).
   - When converting with REAPER's own features, containers other than mp4 / mov / avi (MKV and so on) cannot report their resolution automatically, so a window asking for width, height and frame rate appears (it does not appear when converting with FFmpeg).

### Method B: use the FFmpeg scripts (external tool)

If FFmpeg is installed on the PC, the included scripts can convert to all-intra H.264 (smaller files than MJPEG).

- **Windows**: drag and drop the video file onto `tools/allintra_ffmpeg.cmd`.
- **macOS**: run `chmod +x tools/allintra_ffmpeg.command` once in Terminal, then double-click the file, drag and drop the video into the window that opens, and press Enter.
- Import the resulting `<name>_allintra.mp4` with `reascratch_import_video.lua` (it is all-intra, so no conversion is offered, unless it is taller than the height chosen in setup; then you are asked whether to convert it smaller). The scripts scale videos down to a height of 720 (to change it, edit `MAXH` in the script).

---

### Why MJPEG, not HAP

HAP (a GPU-oriented format used in TouchDesigner and elsewhere) also stores every frame on its own, but this kit does not use it.

- REAPER cannot write HAP. Reading it also needs FFmpeg installed separately (this kit puts working without extra installs first)
- With FFmpeg 9 installed in REAPER, HAP playback once showed red and blue swapped (2026-10-02). When tested again with the same REAPER and FFmpeg, the issue could not be reproduced; the cause is unknown
- For showing in REAPER's video window, MJPEG runs light enough

If you already have HAP videos, the import check reports them as all-intra (they play if REAPER has FFmpeg).
